items.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019
items.q: INTERVIEWER: You said something that reminded me of Joe Williams... [INTERVIEWEE] I hate those microphones.

ctx.x: Israeli Project, we recorded live together actually with the band in the studio as well. And so that was an experience that was magical. But a lot of times we’ll do individual stacks and so each singer will stack four times or three times, or you know, just depending on how big they want the sound, so yeah.

You said something that reminded me of Joe Williams, who I explained had a big role in what we’re doing here. You said, “Sometimes she wants me to pull back.” And we filmed him once in a concert in our hall here, and there’s this moment there where he was singing a ballad and the Count Basie Band is behind him. And he took the microphone, and the microphone was at belt level, right? And he was singing but he was using that microphone to his good effect. And then I thought about a lot of singers nowadays, I see…

I hate those microphones. I hate those microphones and I hate in-ears. I love being able to connect with your audience. The microphones that are here are restricting, honestly. And most of the time when they have those type of mics it’s because they’re doing dance routines and things like that and so they have those mics to not be restricted in that way. But it’s still, again, the emphasis is more on the performance and less on vocally what you’re doing. And so sometimes you have the stems playing in the…
